title: The Siege of Solberg's Bend
subtitle: Monday 24 to Thursday 27 May 1886: Warrants from Rawlins, Sixteen Guns at Dawn, a Burning Hay Wagon and a Man on the Blind Side

setting.name: Solberg's Bend and the middle creek, the last week of May
setting.description: The thirty days run out on Monday 24 May. The warrants come up from Rawlins with a Company rider: nine names, 'cattle theft', signed by a justice of the peace whom the Company pays. On Tuesday the sheriff must decide whether to serve them; that night the dead-list men and their families, twenty-six people, gather at Solberg's Bend, because the grange believes there is safety in numbers. Before dawn on Wednesday 26 May, Cyrus Ballantine, Jubal Stroud, the eight hired gunmen from the Association and eight Company riders under Wade Tolliver, sixteen guns, surround the Bend. With them, not on anyone's payroll, rides Elam Henley, sent by Gideon Sayre to kill Thea Lasker in the confusion. The scenario is a siege: two days of preparation, a dawn of gunfire and smoke, and an afternoon of reckoning. What the party has done in the first two scenarios decides how it goes: a party that turned Tolliver has eight riders who will not fire; a party that proved the hanging was Sayre's has something to show Ballantine; a party that did neither has rifles and a root cellar.
setting.atmosphere: Late spring at its most beautiful, and the dread underneath it. Wild roses on the creek, meadowlarks, cottonwood fluff drifting like snow, the hay meadows knee-high and green. The Bend is a working homestead full of children who have been told to be quiet, women loading rifles and making bread, men digging rifle pits in the garden and arguing. The night before the raid is short and warm and sleepless, with a sky full of stars and dogs barking at nothing. The dawn is grey and still and smells of sage and then of gunsmoke and burning hay. The violence is a western paperback's: loud, fast, frightening and consequential; people are hurt and some may die, and nothing about it is glorious.

keyLocations.name: Solberg's Bend: the house, the barns and the root cellar
keyLocations.description: Margit Solberg's homestead on a wide bend of the creek, the oldest and strongest place in the middle valley: a two-storey frame house with a stone foundation and a kitchen ell, a stone-walled root cellar dug into the hillside behind it, two log hay barns, a horse corral, a chicken house, a windmill and stock tank, and, a hundred yards off by the road, the log grange hall. The creek wraps round it on three sides; on the fourth, the north, a low sagebrush ridge two hundred yards off overlooks everything. Willows along the creek give cover to anyone who wants to come close.
features: The house: thick plank walls that stop a pistol bullet but not a rifle; shuttered windows; the kitchen ell on the east, the blind side from the ridge, where the women and children will shelter
The root cellar: stone walls and an earth roof, a heavy plank door, the safest place on the Bend, big enough for twenty people standing
The hay barns: full of last year's hay, upwind of the house in the morning breeze; if they burn, the smoke blinds the house
The windmill and stock tank: the only water inside the defences; the creek is covered from the willows
The low ridge to the north, two hundred yards off: the raiders' main firing line
encounters: Twenty-six people of the dead-list families: eleven men and boys who can shoot, nine women (six who can shoot), six children under ten
The raiders at dawn: Ballantine, Stroud, eight Association gunmen, Tolliver and eight Company riders, and Elam Henley
secrets: The raiders' plan (CLUE D4, if Tolliver gave it): Stroud and four Association gunmen on the north ridge with rifles; Tolliver's eight riders on the road and the creek ford to cut off escape; four Association gunmen in the willows on the west; Ballantine on the ridge with the warrants and a white flag, to call on the named men to surrender at sunrise. If they do not, the order is to fire the barns with a burning hay wagon pushed down from the ridge and 'take them as they come out'.

CLUE F1: Elam Henley rides with the Association gunmen but is not on the Company's payroll. Tolliver noticed him join at the Forks at midnight and asked who hired him; an Association gunman said 'the boss's friend from town'. Ballantine thinks Stroud hired him; Stroud thinks Ballantine did.

CLUE F2: when the firing starts, Henley does not go to his assigned place in the willows. He works round, under cover of the creek bank, to the east side, the house's blind side, where the kitchen ell is, and where Thea Lasker and the children are. He means to shoot her through the kitchen window and leave in the smoke. A character watching the east side, or anyone with a passive Perception of 15 or more on the house's east side, sees him coming.
Under the kitchen floor is a trap door into a short crawl tunnel to the root cellar that Margit's husband dug in 1880; only Margit and Clara know it is there.

keyLocations.name: The Ransom County courthouse
keyLocations.description: Gilead, Monday 24 and Tuesday 25 May. The warrants arrive at the sheriff's office in a Company rider's saddlebag: nine names, 'theft of neat cattle, the property of the Bitter Creek Land & Cattle Company', sworn before Justice of the Peace Orrin Plum of Rawlins, whom the Company pays $50 a month as 'legal adviser'. Sheriff Quinlan must serve them, or refuse, or find a reason to delay.
features: The sheriff's desk and the warrants, in a blue paper cover
The two iron cells, where Ira Pettit may be sleeping
The clerk's office and the law books: a copy of the territory's compiled laws, which say how a warrant may be challenged
encounters: Sheriff Silas Quinlan, at the end of his excuses
A Company rider, Duncan Lyall carrying Ballantine's letter, and two Association gunmen to see that the warrants are served
secrets: The warrants are defective: Rawlins is in Carbon County, and Ransom County has been a separate county since 1885; a Carbon County justice of the peace has no jurisdiction over theft committed in Ransom County. Anyone who reads the compiled laws (Investigation DC 13) or asks Lavinia Thorpe, Dr. Haskell or Gustav Lindahl finds it. Quinlan can refuse to serve them on that ground and be right; it takes courage, which he does not have unless someone lends him some.
Quinlan owes Beau Fairchild $400 at cards. Beau can forgive the debt, or call it in. Either works as leverage; the first earns Quinlan's loyalty and the second his fear.
CLUE D5: the warrants themselves, sworn on 24 May, nine names, with Ballantine's covering letter: 'Serve these on the 25th. We shall be at the Bend on the 26th whether you are or not.'

keyLocations.name: The north ridge
keyLocations.description: A low sagebrush ridge two hundred yards north of the Solberg house, the only high ground near the Bend. Behind it, out of sight of the house, a dry wash where the raiders leave their horses. The Company's hay wagon, borrowed from the Bend's own neighbour, is parked here before dawn, loaded with hay and a can of coal oil.
features: Rifle positions in the sage, looking down on the house and barns
The dry wash and the horse lines, with two men holding the horses
The hay wagon at the top of the slope, with its tongue lashed for pushing downhill toward the barns
encounters: Jubal Stroud (Fast Gun, with his Buffalo rifle) and four Association gunmen (Hired Gun)
Cyrus Ballantine (Cattle Baron), with the warrants and a white flag
secrets: CLUE C3: Stroud's saddlebag, on his grey horse in the dry wash, holds the Association's annotated dead list: ten names, Owen's struck through, and beside six of them, in the Association secretary's hand, 'per G.S., Gilead', with dates going back to 1884. A character who reaches the horse lines (Stealth DC 15 past the horse holders) can take it. Stroud, if he discovers its loss, will know who 'G.S.' is the moment someone explains it to him.
A party scouting the ridge the night before can disable the hay wagon (cut the lashings, wet the hay, take the coal oil) without anyone knowing until dawn.

keyLocations.name: The Red Breaks: Fergus Mallory's cabin
keyLocations.description: Twelve miles south, a cabin in a box canyon in the clay breaks, found only by following Fergus Mallory or a horse that knows the way. Fergus, the valley's actual rustler and a companion, is on the dead list. He keeps a case of dynamite here 'for prospecting'.
features: A hidden spring and a brush corral full of horses with nobody's brand on them
A case of dynamite, twenty sticks, and a coil of fuse
A view from the canyon rim of the Rawlins road and the whole middle valley
encounters: Fergus Mallory (companion), who would rather not be anywhere near Solberg's Bend on Wednesday
secrets: Fergus saw two riders on the creek road by moonlight on the night Owen was hanged, going toward the Narrows from Gilead: a long man on a bay and a boy. He has told no one, because who would believe a rustler. He will tell the party if they protect him or trust him.
The dynamite is the siege's wild card. Used well, it collapses the creek bank under the willows and cuts the western attackers off; used badly, it kills people.

keyLocations.name: Booker's Draw
keyLocations.description: Calvin Booker's place, two miles south of the Bend, with one narrow mouth between cedar ridges. Booker argues that the families should shelter here, not at the Bend: one way in, easily held. Margit will not leave her home.
features: The narrow mouth, where three rifles could hold off thirty
The trail out the back over the ridge into the Red Breaks
encounters: Calvin Booker (companion), Joe Pruneda with his arm in a sling
secrets: If the party persuades the families to move to Booker's Draw on Tuesday night, Ballantine's raid finds the Bend empty except for whoever stayed to hold it, and must either give up or attack the Draw at noon, uphill, through a gap, against prepared rifles; Tolliver refuses to do that, and the raid falls apart. This is a legitimate and clever solution and the GM should reward it.

synopsis: The thirty days run out. On Monday 24 May warrants for the nine dead-list men arrive in Gilead from a bought justice in Rawlins, and Sheriff Quinlan has a day to decide whether to serve them; the party can find the flaw in them, lend him courage or call in his debts. On Tuesday night the dead-list families gather at Solberg's Bend, and the party has a night to prepare: rifle pits, the root cellar, the hay wagon on the ridge, Fergus Mallory's dynamite, or a move to Booker's Draw. At dawn on Wednesday 26 May, Ballantine, Stroud, the Association gunmen and Tolliver's riders surround the Bend, Ballantine calls on the named men to surrender, and if they will not, the burning hay wagon comes down the slope toward the barns. In the smoke, Elam Henley works round to the house's blind side to kill Thea Lasker, the one person whose claim can undo Sayre's forgery. How the siege goes depends on what the party has done: a turned Tolliver will not fire and may call off his riders; proof of who hanged Owen Lasker, shown to Ballantine under a white flag in front of his own men, can end the raid; Stroud's stolen dead list, with 'per G.S.' beside six names, can turn the Association's own gunman against the man who used its name. In the afternoon the sheriff arrives with a posse, late, and somebody has to decide what happens to the raiders, the warrants, and Henley, if he was taken alive and the grange wants him hanged.
hook: Monday 24 May, noon, the sheriff's office in Gilead. A Company rider puts a blue paper packet on Silas Quinlan's desk and stands there, with two Association gunmen behind him in the doorway, while the sheriff reads nine names. Quinlan looks up at the party, if they are there, or sends a boy to find them if they are not. 'They want me to serve these tomorrow,' he says. 'And they say they'll be at Solberg's Bend Wednesday whether I am or not.'

conclusions.conclusion: F. Henley rides with the raiders to kill Thea Lasker
clues: F1: Henley joined the raiders at the Forks with no one's payroll (Tolliver, the Association gunmen)
F2: in the fight he goes to the house's blind side, not to his post (the Bend)
F3: a widow continuing the claim defeats a forged relinquishment (Thea, Lavinia Thorpe, Judge Kittle)
Henley's own words if taken alive: 'the notary said the widow, and only the widow'

conclusions.conclusion: C. Gideon Sayre paid for the hanging (confirmed)
clues: C3: the Association's annotated dead list, 'per G.S., Gilead' (Stroud's saddlebag)
C6: Henley's confession that 'the notary' paid them (if taken alive)
C2 and C4 from earlier scenarios: the survey payroll and Owen's page
Stroud, once he reads the list and is told who G.S. is

conclusions.conclusion: D. The warrants are the Company's, and they are bad law
clues: D5: the warrants, sworn before a Carbon County justice for a Ransom County offence (the courthouse)
The territory's compiled laws on jurisdiction (the clerk's office, Lavinia, Dr. Haskell)
J.P. Plum's $50 a month from the Company, in Lyall's ledger (the Forks, if visited)

acts.title: Thirty Days
acts.description: Monday 24 and Tuesday 25 May. The warrants arrive; the sheriff must choose; the families gather at the Bend; and the party has one night to prepare. This act is about choices made in advance. Everything the party sets up here, a sheriff who will not serve bad paper, a disabled hay wagon, a tunnel cleared, a move to Booker's Draw, dynamite in the creek bank, a turned Tolliver, pays off at dawn. Let the players plan in detail and reward good plans.
objectives: Persuade, pressure or shame Sheriff Quinlan about the warrants
Decide whether to defend Solberg's Bend, move the families, or meet the raiders elsewhere
Scout the north ridge and the raiders' plan
Prepare the defences: water, the root cellar, the barns, the hay wagon

scenes.name: Bad Paper
scenes.description: The sheriff's office. Quinlan is a decent coward who owes everyone and is about to be made to pay. The warrants are defective (Carbon County J.P., Ransom County offence); the party can find this, or Lavinia Thorpe can, or Dr. Haskell, or Gustav Lindahl. Ezra Langford, if played, is a deputy and must decide whether to carry them. Beau Fairchild, if played, holds Quinlan's $400 in IOUs. The scene's question: will the law of Ransom County serve the Company's warrants? If Quinlan refuses, the raid goes ahead anyway, but without any colour of law, and every raider is a common criminal; Tolliver's riders know it, and so does Judge Kittle when he arrives in June. If Quinlan serves them, he rides out to the Bend on Tuesday, reads them aloud, is refused, and rides back, and the raid has a warrant to wave.
scenes.readAloud: Silas Quinlan has taken his badge off and laid it on the desk next to the blue paper packet, and he is looking at both of them as if he could not decide which one was going to bite him. The Company rider has gone to the Antelope for a drink. The two Association gunmen are sitting on the bench outside the office window, in the sun, smoking, where the sheriff can see them. 'Nine names,' Quinlan says. 'Booker. Solberg's boy. The Kettlesons. Mallory, if anyone can find him. Theft of neat cattle. Signed by Orrin Plum of Rawlins, Justice of the Peace.' He rubs his face. 'I got elected with Ballantine's five hundred dollars and those people's votes. I've got a wife and a mortgage and I'm fifty-five years old. You tell me what I'm supposed to do.'

skillChecks.success: In the compiled laws on the clerk's shelf: a justice of the peace's warrant runs within his own county. Rawlins is in Carbon County; Ransom County was organised in 1885; the alleged thefts were in Ransom County. Plum had no jurisdiction. The warrants are void. Quinlan stares at the page, then laughs out loud, the first time anyone has heard him laugh since April.
skillChecks.failure: The law books are long and the type is small. You know there is something wrong with these warrants and cannot find it in time; Lavinia Thorpe might.

skillChecks.success: You lend Quinlan the courage he does not have. He puts his badge back on, walks out to the bench and tells the two Association gunmen that Ransom County does not serve Carbon County paper, and that any man who rides on Solberg's Bend will answer to the district court. They laugh, but they ride to the Forks to tell Ballantine, and Tolliver hears it. Reputation +1; and the raid, if it comes, comes outside the law.
skillChecks.failure: He wants to, and cannot. 'I'll ride out tomorrow and read them,' he says, 'and I'll tell those people to come in peaceable, and that's all I can do.'

skillChecks.success: You remind him whom he owes, and what happens to sheriffs who ride with raiders when the judge comes. He will not serve the warrants, and he will hate you a little for making him brave. (Beau Fairchild may simply tear up the IOUs in front of him instead, which does the same thing and earns his gratitude.)
skillChecks.failure: Quinlan pins his badge back on with shaking fingers and says he will do his duty, whatever that is. He does not know either.

scenes.name: Twenty-Six People
scenes.description: Tuesday evening at Solberg's Bend. The dead-list families arrive in wagons and on horseback, with bedding, rifles, dogs, a crate of chickens and a cradle: twenty-six people. Margit is back from Cheyenne with a letter from the governor's secretary that says nothing. Calvin Booker argues for moving everyone to Booker's Draw. Margit will not leave the home she built. Nils wants to ride out and fight on the road. Thea Lasker is there with Pete. The party's job is to turn a frightened crowd into a defence, or a column on the move. Play the domestic details: a woman making bread because there will be people to feed tomorrow, children told to play quietly, men digging rifle pits in the potato patch, a boy of twelve asking for a gun.
scenes.readAloud: They come all evening, up the creek road and down from the side draws, in wagons with their bedding and their rifles and their children: the Kettleson brothers and their wives, old Wiley Dorsett's family, Lars Engstrom with an axe and a shotgun, Calvin Booker and Joe Pruneda with his arm in a sling, Thea Lasker with Pete on her hip. Twenty-six people. Margit Solberg stands in her kitchen doorway in a floury apron and greets every one of them by name and finds them a place to put their blankets, as if this were a harvest supper. Out in the potato patch, by lantern light, men are digging. In the parlour, someone has started to sing a Norwegian hymn, and stopped, and started again. Everyone keeps looking at the low ridge to the north, black against the last of the light.

skillChecks.success: You persuade Margit, which persuades everyone: the families go to Booker's Draw tonight, by the creek and the back trail, and only a dozen volunteers stay at the Bend to make it look held. At dawn the raiders find the Bend nearly empty and the Draw impregnable. Tolliver refuses to lead his men up the gap. The raid falls apart without a fight worth the name.
skillChecks.failure: Margit will not leave. 'My husband is buried on that hill,' she says. 'I am not leaving him to the Company.' Those who stay, stay with her.

skillChecks.success: You lay out a real defence: water drawn from the windmill in every tub and barrel; the children and women who cannot shoot in the root cellar before dawn; rifle pits in the potato patch covering the willows; the barns' hay wetted down, or forked out away from the house; lamps out; a watch on the east side. The defenders have advantage on initiative at dawn and the burning wagon will not reach the house.
skillChecks.failure: There are too many people and too many opinions. At dawn half the defenders are asleep, the barns are full of dry hay, and the watch is on the wrong side.

skillChecks.success: Thea Lasker is afraid of something specific. If asked, she says that Gideon Sayre came to see her on Sunday, kindly, to ask whether she 'still meant to contest Owen's relinquishment'. She said she did. He said that was brave of her. (CLUE F3; and a reason to put Thea somewhere no one can reach her.)
skillChecks.failure: Everyone is afraid. Thea is quiet and steady and helps Margit with the bread.

scenes.name: The Ridge at Night
scenes.description: Tuesday night, late. A party that scouts the north ridge and the dry wash behind it after midnight finds the raiders arriving: sixteen men and a hay wagon, horses on a line in the wash, no fires. With them, apart, a long man on a bay with a bar shoe. A party that is quiet can listen to Ballantine giving orders, disable the hay wagon, steal Stroud's saddlebag from his grey horse, speak to Tolliver alone in the dark, or simply count. This scene is the siege's hidden key: what the party does here decides whether dawn is a massacre, a standoff or a parley.
scenes.readAloud: The ridge is black and silent and smells of sage and horse. Below it, in the dry wash, there are no fires, only the shapes of horses on a picket line, the creak of leather, a cough quickly muffled, the red point of a cigarette cupped in a hand. Sixteen men, maybe more. A wagon stands at the top of the slope, piled high with hay, and a man is lashing its tongue so it will roll. In the starlight a tall rider on a grey horse walks it along the line of men and says something low, and they laugh. And apart from all of them, a long man on a bay horse sits his saddle and looks down at the dark shape of the Solberg house, and does not laugh with anyone.

skillChecks.success: You reach the horse lines unseen. In Stroud's saddlebag, wrapped in oilcloth: the Association's annotated dead list, with 'per G.S., Gilead' beside six names (CLUE C3). You could also cut the hay wagon's lashings or pour its coal oil into the sand, and be back over the ridge before anyone looks.
skillChecks.failure: A horse holder hears you and calls out. You are not seen, but the raiders double the guard on the horses and the wagon, and Stroud walks the ridge for an hour with his rifle.

skillChecks.success: You see Henley, and see that he is not with the Association gunmen or with Tolliver's riders; he is alone, and he keeps looking at the house's east side, where the kitchen ell is (CLUE F1). Someone should be watching that side at dawn.
skillChecks.failure: Men and horses in the dark. You count fourteen, maybe sixteen. You do not see the bay with the bar shoe.

skillChecks.success: You find Wade Tolliver alone at the end of the horse line and speak to him in the dark. If you have proof (the payroll, Pettit, the sign), he takes it in, and says: 'My boys won't fire on women. If Ballantine sends the wagon down, I'll stop it. That's all I can promise.' If you have the dead list, he reads 'per G.S.' by starlight and swears softly.
skillChecks.failure: Tolliver tells you to get off the ridge before Stroud sees you, and means it kindly.

encounters: No set combat. The two Association gunmen at the courthouse (Hired Gun) start trouble only if the party does
On the ridge at night, two horse holders (Hired Gun) and a sentry; a fight here alerts the raid and brings it forward to darkness, which is worse for everyone

acts.title: Dawn at Solberg's Bend
acts.description: Wednesday 26 May, first light. The siege. Ballantine comes down the slope under a white flag with the warrants and calls on the nine named men to come out and surrender. Then, if they do not, the shooting starts, and the burning hay wagon comes down toward the barns. Somewhere in the smoke Henley is working round to the blind side. Run this as the campaign's biggest set piece, in rounds when it is combat and in minutes when it is not, and let the party's preparations show: everything they set up last night happens now.
objectives: Answer Ballantine's parley, and use it if the party has proof
Hold the house, the root cellar and the water
Stop Elam Henley before he reaches Thea Lasker

scenes.name: The White Flag
scenes.description: Sunrise. Ballantine walks his horse down the slope with Stroud beside him and a white handkerchief on a carbine barrel, stops at a hundred yards, and calls for the nine named men to come out with their hands up and be taken to Rawlins for trial. This is the party's best chance to end the siege without a shot: in front of his own men, Ballantine can be shown that the warrants are void, that Owen Lasker was hanged by Sayre's hirelings, that the Company has been used, and that the district judge will be in Gilead in twelve days. He is a cold man but not a stupid one; proof shown in front of Tolliver's riders and the Association gunmen, with Tolliver backing it, makes the raid more expensive than it is worth. Stroud, shown the annotated dead list and told who G.S. is, turns his horse round and rides back up the ridge without a word: he has somewhere else to be. Without proof, the parley is a formality, and the named men refuse.
scenes.readAloud: The sun comes up behind the ridge and lights the cottonwoods along the creek gold, and a meadowlark starts singing on the windmill as if nothing were wrong. Then two riders come over the crest and walk their horses down the slope through the wet sage: a straight grey man in a black coat with a white handkerchief tied to a carbine barrel, and beside him on a tall grey horse a lean man in a grey coat with a rifle across his saddle. They stop at a hundred yards. Behind them, along the ridge, rifle barrels catch the light, one, five, a dozen. 'This is Cyrus Ballantine,' calls the grey man, in a clear Scots voice. 'I have warrants for nine men in that house. I'll read the names. Let them come out with their hands empty and no one need be hurt. You have until I have finished reading.'

skillChecks.success: With proof in your hand (the payroll book, Pettit, the void warrants, the dead list), you walk out to meet him and lay it out where Tolliver and his riders can hear. Ballantine listens without expression. Then he asks to see the jurisdiction point in writing, reads it, folds it, and says, 'Mr. Tolliver, take your men home.' The Association gunmen look at Stroud; Stroud is looking at the dead list. The raid is over. (Without proof the DC is 22, and even success only buys an hour.)
skillChecks.failure: Ballantine hears you out, says 'that is a matter for a court', and reads the first name. The named men will not come out. When he finishes reading, he turns his horse.

skillChecks.success: You tell Ballantine, loudly enough for the ridge to hear, exactly what will happen to every man up there when Judge Kittle opens court on 7 June, and you name the ones you recognise. Two of Tolliver's riders slip away over the crest before the shooting starts, and the Company side has disadvantage on its first round of fire.
skillChecks.failure: Stroud smiles at you across a hundred yards of sage. 'Brave,' he says. 'Let's see.'

skillChecks.success: Ballantine does not want this. He wants it done, which is different. He would take a way out that let him keep his dignity in front of his investors. Stroud wants the fight, and is watching you to see who will start it. And someone on the ridge has a pair of field glasses trained not on the house's front, but on its east side.
skillChecks.failure: Two hard men under a white flag. You cannot read past it.

scenes.name: The Burning Wagon
scenes.description: If the parley fails, the shooting starts: Stroud and four Association gunmen from the ridge, four more in the willows on the west, Tolliver's riders on the road and the ford (and whether they fire depends on bk-scenario-002). Then the hay wagon comes down the slope, pushed by four men, blazing, toward the barns upwind of the house. If the barns catch, the smoke blinds the house, and the raiders close in under it. Stopping the wagon is the scene's heroics: shoot the men pushing it, shoot the wagon's wheel off (AC 15, 20 hp), ride out and rope its tongue and drag it off line (a Cowhand's Saddle-Born, Riding DC 15), or blow the slope in front of it with Fergus's dynamite. Use combat.json's cover rules for the house, rifle pits, the stock tank and the stone root cellar, and keep the fight moving: in rounds when it is close, in minutes when the two sides are trading long shots.
scenes.readAloud: The first shot comes from the ridge as the last name is read, a heavy flat boom from a buffalo rifle that knocks a shutter off the parlour window, and then the whole ridge opens up, a ragged rolling crackle, and bullets are going through the house's plank walls with a sound like someone hitting a barrel with a stick. Glass everywhere. A child screaming in the root cellar and being hushed. Smoke from your own rifles filling the room. And then, on the ridge, a shout, and the hay wagon comes over the crest and down the slope, four men running behind it and pushing and then letting it go, and as it gathers speed someone throws a lantern into it, and it goes up all at once, a rolling bonfire bouncing and roaring down through the sage, straight at the big hay barn and the house behind it.

skillChecks.success: You ride out under fire, get a rope on the burning wagon's tongue, and drag it off line into the creek in a cloud of steam. Every rifle on the ridge is shooting at you and none of them hits. The defenders cheer. Reputation +1 when the story is told, and it will be.
skillChecks.failure: You get the rope on and your horse will not face the fire; you are dragged a dozen yards and must let go (2d6 bludgeoning, DEX save DC 13 for half). The wagon goes on toward the barn.

skillChecks.success: With Fergus's dynamite, you cut a fuse to the second and bury two sticks in the slope in front of the wagon; the blast throws up a wall of earth that stops it dead and burns out harmlessly. The four men pushing it run.
skillChecks.failure: The fuse is too long, or too short. The dynamite goes off behind the wagon, or under it, scattering burning hay across the slope and into the sage. Nobody on your side is hurt, but the grass fire is now between you and the ridge.

skillChecks.success: With three others, you get the big barn's hay forked out and wetted, or the barn doors shut and the roof soaked from the stock tank, before the wagon arrives. It burns against the barn wall and goes out. The house is not blinded.
skillChecks.failure: The barn catches. Smoke rolls over the house; the defenders are blinded (heavily obscured) for ten rounds, and the raiders in the willows start forward under it.

scenes.name: The Blind Side
scenes.description: In the smoke and noise, Elam Henley comes along the creek bank under the willows to the house's east side, the kitchen ell, where Thea Lasker is (unless the party moved her to the root cellar or the tunnel). He means to shoot her through the kitchen window, or, if she is in the root cellar, to fire the cellar door. A character watching the east side sees him; otherwise, give the party a Perception check. This is a short, personal fight in a kitchen or a yard full of smoke: Henley is an Outlaw with an Army revolver and nothing to lose. If he is taken alive, he is the second hangman and the second witness against Sayre; if he is killed, the party has saved Thea and lost a voice. If he gets away, he rides for Gilead and Sayre.
scenes.readAloud: Under the gunfire, in the kitchen, you hear something that should not be there: a boot on the gravel of the creek bank, close, on the side away from the ridge, where nobody should be. Then a long shadow across the kitchen window, through the smoke, and the window's lower pane goes out in a spray of glass, and a revolver barrel comes in through it, and behind it a long lantern-jawed face that you have seen before, at a corner table in the Antelope, grinning. He is not looking at you. He is looking past you, into the corner by the stove, where Thea Lasker is crouched with her arms round her son.

skillChecks.success: You hear him coming before he reaches the window, and you are in the kitchen with your gun out when the glass breaks. You act first. (Automatic if the party set a watch on the east side.)
skillChecks.failure: The glass breaks and he fires before anyone moves: the shot is at Thea (AC 10, 9 hp); roll it. Then initiative.

skillChecks.success: With your gun on him from two yards, you tell him to drop it, and he believes you. He drops it, puts his hands on the sill, and says, 'I want a lawyer. And I want the notary hanged first.' (CLUES B6, C6)
skillChecks.failure: He sneers and swings the revolver toward you. It is a fight now.

skillChecks.success: If he runs, you track the bay with the bar shoe along the creek through the smoke and catch him at the ford, where his horse balks at the water. He fights or surrenders there.
skillChecks.failure: He is gone into the willows and the smoke, and an hour later a bay horse with a bar shoe is seen on the Gilead road at a dead run.

encounters: The siege: Jubal Stroud (Fast Gun) and four Association gunmen (Hired Gun) on the north ridge at 200 yards; four Association gunmen (Hired Gun) in the west willows; Wade Tolliver (Range Boss) and eight Company riders (use Deputy or Hired Gun) on the road and ford, who may not fire at all; Cyrus Ballantine (Cattle Baron) directing. Defenders have cover in the house (three-quarters behind the stone foundation, half behind plank walls), the rifle pits, the stock tank and the root cellar
The burning hay wagon: a hazard; 4d6 fire damage to anything it hits, and the barns catch in 1d4 rounds
Elam Henley (Outlaw) at the kitchen window or the root cellar door

acts.title: After the Smoke
acts.description: Wednesday afternoon to Thursday 27 May. However the siege ended, by parley, by fight or by evasion, there are consequences to deal with: wounded on both sides, perhaps dead; prisoners; Sheriff Quinlan arriving at noon with a posse of townsmen, late; Stroud gone somewhere with the dead list (or without it); Henley in a cell, or dead, or riding for Gilead; and twenty-six frightened people who now know, or will soon, who hanged Owen Lasker. The act ends with the grange's anger turning toward Gilead, and Sayre.
objectives: Tend the wounded on both sides
Hand prisoners to the law, and keep them alive
Decide what to tell the grange about Sayre, and when
Make sure Gideon Sayre does not get away before the judge comes

scenes.name: Noon
scenes.description: Sheriff Quinlan arrives at noon with eleven townsmen sworn as a posse: too late to stop anything, in time to take charge of whatever is left. If Quinlan refused to serve the warrants, he arrests any raiders still at the Bend for riot and assault, and Ballantine, if present, surrenders with dignity and is released on bond by evening; the Company's lawyers in Laramie will be in Gilead by the judge's term. If Quinlan served them, he is ashamed and confused, and the party has to tell him what really happened. Dr. Haskell comes with him and works on the wounded of both sides in Margit's parlour. This is a quiet, painful scene of cost: who is hurt, who is dead, what the house looks like, what the children saw.
scenes.readAloud: The posse comes up the creek road at noon at a trot, eleven men from Gilead on livery horses with shotguns and borrowed rifles and the sheriff at their head, and they rein in at the gate and look at what is there: the smashed windows, the black scar on the slope where the wagon burned, the barn smoking or not, the bullet-pocked walls, the wounded laid out on blankets in the shade of the windmill, and the people of Solberg's Bend standing in the yard looking back at them. Nobody says anything for a while. Then Dr. Abigail Haskell gets down from the buggy behind the posse with her bag, says 'Well. Where are they?' in a voice like a slammed door, and goes into the house, and the silence breaks.

skillChecks.success: You work beside Dr. Haskell until dark and between you nobody else dies, including two Association gunmen and a Company boy shot in the willows. Word of that goes to the Forks. Company attitude +1; Reputation +1.
skillChecks.failure: You do what you can. One of the wounded, the GM's choice and preferably from the side the party did not fight for, dies at sunset.

skillChecks.success: You get Quinlan to take every prisoner to Gilead under the posse's guard and to wire nobody until the judge comes, so that the Company's lawyers and the Association do not hear the full story first. He agrees, and asks you to ride with him.
skillChecks.failure: Quinlan wants to release everyone on their own word and 'let the judge sort it out'. The Association gunmen are gone by morning.

skillChecks.success: Margit Solberg, watching the posse, knows now. She has seen Henley, or heard what he said, or read 'per G.S.' in the list. She sits down on the step of her ruined kitchen and says, quietly, 'He was our secretary. He wrote our minutes. He gave us the name of the grange.' Then she says, 'Nils must not know yet.'
skillChecks.failure: Everyone is exhausted. Nobody is thinking past tonight.

scenes.name: The Grey Horse
scenes.description: If the party gave Stroud the dead list's meaning (or he worked it out from what he heard in the parley), he rides away from the Bend at midday alone toward Gilead. Stroud's code is offended: a clerk used his Association's name on a hanging and sold names that put Stroud's own reputation behind it. He means to call Sayre out in the street, or simply to shoot him. The party may want that. They may not: a dead Sayre cannot be tried, the forged relinquishment may never be proved, and Thea's claim depends on it. Catching Stroud on the Gilead road is a chase on horseback and a conversation with a man who will draw if crowded. Persuading him to wait for the judge, or to testify instead, is the hardest Persuasion in the campaign. If nobody intervenes, Stroud reaches Gilead on Thursday morning, and Sayre, warned by Henley or by the sight of the grey horse on the road, has barricaded himself in his office with the evidence and a shotgun; the scene becomes bk-scenario-004's opening.
scenes.readAloud: He rides away from the Bend at noon at a walk, the grey horse picking its way down through the burned sage, and he does not look back at any of it, the house, the wounded, his own Association gunmen, Ballantine calling after him. On the Gilead road he lifts the grey into a long easy lope that will eat the nine miles in an hour. If you ride hard you can catch him at the creek bridge below Gilead, where the road narrows and a man has to stop. He is waiting for you there, sitting the grey in the middle of the bridge with his hands crossed on the horn. 'I know what you want to say,' Jubal Stroud says. 'Say it anyway.'

skillChecks.success: You persuade him that a man of rules lets the court hang Sayre, and that the papers will say Jubal Stroud gave the evidence that did it. He thinks about it a long time. Then he hands you the dead list, if he had it, and says, 'I'll be at the Ransom House when the judge comes. If he lets the notary walk, I won't.' (Stroud becomes a witness in bk-scenario-004, and a threat.)
skillChecks.failure: He listens, and shakes his head. 'You want him tried. I want him dead. We can both have what we want if you get out of my road.'

skillChecks.success: His pride is the lever: he cannot bear to be thought an amateur, a hangman, a man who uses signs. Give him a way to be the professional who brought the real hangman to book, and he may take it.
skillChecks.failure: His face tells you nothing at all. It never has.

skillChecks.success: In a stare-down on the bridge, you hold his eyes until he looks away, and he says, 'All right. Your way. For now.' (Use the showdown rules for the stare-down; the loser may back down with their life.)
skillChecks.failure: He offers you the draw, here, now, on the bridge. You may back down with your life (Reputation -1), or face him. At level 4 or 5 this is a real chance of death, and the GM should say so.

scenes.name: The Secretary's Minutes
scenes.description: Thursday 27 May. The grange, or what is left of it, meets in the battered grange hall to hear what happened. Someone has to tell them about Sayre. Nils Solberg, when he hears, takes his carbine off the wall. The party now faces the campaign's last moral question in miniature: they have the evidence to see Gideon Sayre hanged by law, and a valley full of people who would rather do it themselves tonight. Judge Kittle is due on 7 June. Sayre is in his office in Gilead, a federal officer, with the township records and, he believes, every friend he has ever made by being helpful. What does the party do for the next ten days? Guard Sayre? Guard the evidence? Guard Henley? Telegraph Cheyenne from Rawlins? Tell Lavinia Thorpe? The scenario ends with that choice, and with the Plainsman's headline.
scenes.readAloud: The grange hall has eleven bullet holes in its north wall and the blue and gold banner has one through the sheaf of wheat. Someone has swept up the glass. They come anyway, the ones who can, and sit on the benches in their bandages and their Sunday coats, and the secretary's little table on the platform is empty, with the minute book lying on it, closed. Margit Solberg stands behind the table and does not use her gavel. 'Before we vote on anything,' she says, 'these people have something to tell us about Owen. And about Mr. Sayre.' At the back of the hall, Nils Solberg stands up very slowly, and his hand goes to the rifle leaning against the wall beside him.

skillChecks.success: You tell them the truth and then you tell them why it must go to the judge: because a hanging is what Sayre did to Owen, because Thea's claim needs a court to void the forgery, and because the grange is not the Company. Margit backs you. Nils sits down, shaking, and gives you his rifle to hold. The grange votes to send a delegation to meet Judge Kittle's stage. Reputation +1.
skillChecks.failure: They hear the truth and the hall erupts. By midnight, forty men are riding for Gilead to take Sayre out of his office; the party has a few hours' head start to get there first. bk-scenario-004 opens with a mob in the street.

skillChecks.success: A sermon, a speech or a story that holds a frightened room: the grange is quiet long enough to think. A Preacher's Fire and Brimstone works here, to steady them or to shame them.
skillChecks.failure: Your words make them angrier, not calmer. Someone shouts 'tonight', and others take it up.

skillChecks.success: Not everyone in the hall is surprised. Two grangers who sold their claims to Sayre's dummy entrymen last year, cheap, when they were frightened off, sit very still. Sayre has done this before: there are four other quarter-sections on the creek in his entrymen's names. That is for the judge too.
skillChecks.failure: Everyone is angry. You cannot tell who is angrier than they should be.

encounters: Jubal Stroud (Fast Gun) on the Gilead bridge: a showdown if the party forces one, and it should be his choice of ground
Elam Henley (Outlaw), if he escaped, at large; he rides for Sayre
No combat at the grange meeting unless the party lets it come to that

npcsInvolved.name: Margit Solberg, 52
npcsInvolved.role: Worthy Master of the grange; owner of the Bend
npcsInvolved.description: Grey, broad, strong-handed, floury apron, careful English. Came out from Norway in 1879 with a husband who is buried on the hill behind the house.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To hold her home, keep her son alive, and keep the grange from becoming what it is fighting.

npcsInvolved.name: Sheriff Silas Quinlan, 55
npcsInvolved.role: Sheriff of Ransom County, at the end of his excuses
npcsInvolved.description: Stout, grey, tired, kindly, frightened. Owes the Company $500, the grange its votes and Beau Fairchild $400.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Not to choose. If made to, to choose the side that lets him look at himself in the mirror.

npcsInvolved.name: Cyrus Ballantine, 51
npcsInvolved.role: The Company's manager, leading the raid
npcsInvolved.description: Grey, straight, Scots, a white handkerchief on a carbine barrel.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To clear the creek and answer to Edinburgh. He does not enjoy this; he will stop if it becomes too expensive.

npcsInvolved.name: Jubal Stroud, 40
npcsInvolved.role: The Association's gunman; the raid's real commander
npcsInvolved.description: Lean, grey coat, a Buffalo rifle on the ridge and an Army revolver for close work.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The work, and his name. Once he knows who used it, he wants Gideon Sayre more than anyone on the dead list.

npcsInvolved.name: Wade Tolliver, 46
npcsInvolved.role: Range boss, leading eight Company riders
npcsInvolved.description: Big, sheepskin coat, a bad night behind him.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Whatever he decided at his fire in bk-scenario-002. His riders do what he does.

npcsInvolved.name: Elam Henley, 34
npcsInvolved.role: Sayre's man in the raid; Thea's would-be killer
npcsInvolved.description: Long, lantern-jawed, a bay with a bar shoe, an Army revolver.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To kill Thea Lasker in the confusion, collect from Sayre, and be gone.

npcsInvolved.name: Thea Lasker, 27
npcsInvolved.description: Thin, steady, a rifle she can use, Pete on her hip.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To live long enough to contest the relinquishment, and to see Pete grow up on the Narrows.

npcsInvolved.name: Nils Solberg, 24
npcsInvolved.role: Margit's son; on the dead list
npcsInvolved.description: Tall, fair, a carbine, a grief, and a new and terrible piece of knowledge.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To hang the man who had Owen hanged. The campaign's last test is whether anyone can stop him.

npcsInvolved.name: Justice of the Peace Orrin Plum (offstage)
npcsInvolved.role: The Rawlins J.P. who swore the warrants
npcsInvolved.description: Never seen; a name on a blue paper cover and a line in the Company's ledger at $50 a month.

rewards.money: The grange pays what it promised and more if the Bend stood: $50 a head from a collection taken in a hat. A party working for the Company that refused to fire on the Bend is fired, and paid to the day. Tolliver, if turned, quietly gives each party member a good horse from the remuda. Whatever is found on dead or captured raiders (about $30 each, and Association commissions) is evidence for the judge.
items: The Association's annotated dead list, 'per G.S., Gilead' (CLUE C3), from Stroud's saddlebag or from Stroud himself
The void warrants and Ballantine's covering letter (CLUE D5)
Elam Henley, alive and in irons, if taken, with his statement that 'the notary said the widow, and only the widow' (CLUES B6, C6, F2)
Henley's Army revolver and the bay with the bar shoe
Margit Solberg's blue and gold grange banner, with a bullet hole through the sheaf, which she gives to the party if they saved the Bend
A list of four other quarter-sections on the creek held by Sayre's dummy entrymen

twists: Elam Henley is not on anyone's payroll in the raid. Ballantine thinks Stroud hired him; Stroud thinks Ballantine did; neither cares enough to ask. A party that asks both will find the answer in the gap between them.

The warrants are void for want of jurisdiction. A sheriff who refuses to serve them on that ground is right, and makes every raider at the Bend an outlaw under the territory's own law, which Judge Kittle will remember on 7 June.

The safest place for the families is not the Bend but Booker's Draw. A party that persuades them to move fights almost nothing, and the raid collapses in humiliation. Reward the clever solution as fully as the heroic one.

Once Stroud knows who G.S. is, he becomes the most dangerous man in the valley for Gideon Sayre, and therefore a danger to the party's case: a dead Sayre cannot be tried, and the forgery may never be formally voided.

Sayre has done this before: four other quarter-sections on the creek are held by his dummy entrymen, bought cheap from homesteaders frightened off by Stroud's cards over two years. Every name he sold the Association was a claim he hoped to buy.
dmTips: Spend the first act letting the players plan. A siege is only as exciting as the preparations make it: let them place rifle pits, draw water, choose who goes in the root cellar, scout the ridge. Then let every preparation matter at dawn.

The siege should not be a massacre unless the party's choices make it one. With Tolliver turned and the warrants exposed, it can end at the white flag. With nothing, it is a hard fight against sixteen guns, and the defenders should take casualties.
Run long-range rifle fire in minutes, not rounds, until someone does something decisive (the wagon, a charge, Henley). Then drop into rounds.

Henley at the kitchen window is the scenario's real climax. Make sure someone is in a position to see him, or give a Perception check; and if Thea is hurt, it must be because the party left her exposed, not because the dice were unkind once.
The grey horse on the Gilead road is optional and powerful. If the party gave Stroud the truth, he goes for Sayre. Let the players feel the temptation of letting him.

End with the grange meeting and the choice about Sayre. Then summarise the ten days to 7 June: the Company's lawyers on the Rawlins stage, Lavinia's headlines, the railroad's land agent on his way, and Sayre in his office with the blinds down.
Lynching is a crime and a horror, never justice. The grange wanting to hang Sayre is human and understandable, and it is exactly what Sayre did to Owen. Make the players hold both of those thoughts.
